# Contributing to spectral-init

## Layout

The repository is a Cargo workspace with three packages:

| Package | Path | Published | Purpose |
|---------|------|-----------|---------|
| `spectral-init` | `.` | yes | The library: `src/`, `examples/`, `tests/` |
| `trustworthiness` | `trustworthiness/` | no | Embedding-quality metric and command-line tools |
| `spectral-init-eval` | `eval/` | no | Research harness: benchmarks, sweeps, exporters |

`research/` holds experiment artifacts and is not built by Cargo.

## Building and testing

The minimum supported Rust version of the library is 1.88. `Cargo.lock` is tracked; pass
`--locked` so that a build never changes it.

```sh
# The whole workspace, as CI runs it (needs cargo-nextest).
cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --all-features --profile ci

# Doctests, including the snippets of README.md and docs/*.md.
cargo test --locked --workspace --doc
```

`cargo test` on its own runs only the library's default-feature tests. The tests of its
internals are in `tests/internals/` and need the hidden `__internal` feature, which
`--all-features` switches on.

The `ci` profile leaves out a few slow tests; two of them run with `--profile slow`.

## Checks

A change has to pass the checks CI runs:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check

# The build users compile, and the whole workspace.
cargo clippy --locked -p spectral-init --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

# Rustdoc without warnings.
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p spectral-init

# The library neither prints nor reads the environment; see the script for the rest.
.github/scripts/check-purity.sh

# The packaged crate contains exactly the allow-listed files and passes its own tests.
.github/scripts/check-package.sh

# The hashes in docs/katex-header.html match the files they refer to.
.github/scripts/check-sri.sh

# Advisories, licenses and duplicate versions (cargo-deny); unused dependencies
# (cargo-machete).
cargo deny --workspace --config .config/deny.toml check
cargo machete
```

`check-package.sh` compares `cargo package --list` with `.github/package-allowlist.txt`.
Add a line there when you add a file under `src/` or `examples/`, or change `include` in
`Cargo.toml`.

### Public API

The public API of the library is recorded in `.github/api-snapshot.txt` and checked by
`.github/scripts/check-api.sh`, which needs a nightly toolchain and
[`cargo-public-api`](https://crates.io/crates/cargo-public-api). The listing depends on
both versions; use the ones CI pins in `.github/workflows/`. After an intended change of
the API, run `.github/scripts/check-api.sh --update` and commit the snapshot.

Everything under `spectral_init::__internal` is outside the public API. It exists for
the tests in `tests/internals/` and for `eval/`, and the `__internal` feature must not
change what the library computes.

## The parity rule

`ComputeMode::PythonCompat` is the reference-matching implementation: its results are
tested against values recorded from umap-learn. A change that could make results diverge
from umap-learn — a different summation order, a different solver path, a SIMD kernel —
belongs behind `ComputeMode::RustNative` and must leave the `PythonCompat` path as it
is.

Numerical changes come with numerical tests: compare against the reference fixtures, up
to the sign of each eigenvector, and use residuals and subspace comparison where
eigenvalues nearly coincide.

## Reference fixtures

`tests/fixtures/` holds `.npz` files generated by umap-learn for nine datasets, and they
are tracked. `tests/README.md` describes their format and how to regenerate them:

```sh
micromamba create -f tests/environment.yml
micromamba activate spectral-test
python tests/generate_fixtures.py --verify
```

Regenerate them only on purpose, for example for a new umap-learn version, and commit
the result together with `tests/fixtures/manifest.json`.

## Unsafe code

The only `unsafe` code of the library is the AVX2 kernel in `src/operator.rs`. Every
`unsafe` block needs a `// SAFETY:` comment, and every safe function that reaches one
has to enforce what the block relies on. The kernel's tests run under Miri in CI.
